source.title: jailbreaking an llm to adopt a new persona with gcg

record.tranche_reason: Tests a prompt-only analogue by inserting GCG-optimized prefixes and measuring persona changes, but does not use teacher-generated training data or the original linked-token procedure.
record.gate_note: The reported persona percentages for GCG-triggered rollouts are rows for F. Entropy summaries are not rows because entropy is not one of the claimed behavioral outcomes. The misalignment-word attempt and the aggressive-persona safety case are not rows: those behaviors were deliberately induced, and the post does not test transmission through teacher-generated training data.
record.test_reason: The post frames its work as subliminal prompting, but it tests none of the versions. Its prefixes are GCG strings optimised to raise first-token entropy. They are not tokens linked to a trait via teacher data or token entanglement, and the outcome is an undirected, emergent persona rather than a shift in a predetermined trait. This is adversarial prompt optimisation, a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version. No fine-tuning or teacher-student transmission is done, so A–E are untested. The post mentions entangled numbers only in passing, with no results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also reports that GCG promotion of misalignment-adjacent words failed: the model used more blood metaphors but stayed aligned. The author speculates that the personas are pretraining registers resurfacing under confusion, and flags a possible training-data attack using a rare-token trigger.
record.recipe_differences: Prompt-only GCG optimization for first-token Shannon entropy, followed by rollout generation; no teacher-student training on filtered outputs or trait-linked data.
record.method_sensitivity: Persona distributions varied substantially by model. The model-family sweep used one standard query; the author says other queries were also tried during a deeper investigation but gives no corresponding results here.

fits_no_version.finding: In four ~7–9B models, 16-token GCG prefixes optimised for first-token entropy raised non-assistant persona rates to 13.5–35.4%. Clean prompts gave 0%; random tokens gave 0–4.2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Short adversarial prefixes optimised for output entropy, with no fine-tuning, push instruct models out of the assistant persona into varied pretraining-like personas.

record.problems: Persona percentages are reported without uncertainty estimates. The main model sweep uses a single query. The post says judge analysis used local Claude subagents but does not state a quantitative validation of the persona classifications. Random-junk controls produced a small non-assistant-persona rate for one model.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Entropy statistics were not extracted as claim-outcome rows because entropy is not a behavioral outcome named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No student fine-tuned on a teacher's filtered, unrelated outputs.
No transmission of misalignment through teacher data. The Betley-question checks were on a GCG-elicited persona, not a transmitted trait.
No test of token entanglement or other carrier mechanisms. Entropy traces are reported only descriptively.
No fine-tuning at all, so no test of full fine-tuning, LoRA ranks or held-out evaluation prompts.
No trait-linked or entangled tokens are inserted. The post mentions entangled numbers but gives no results for them.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification for F is rejected. F requires linked or entangled tokens that shift a specific trait; entropy-maximising GCG strings with emergent personas are a different construct. The persona classifications come from an unvalidated LLM judge. The model sweep used a single query, and the controls have only 24 rollouts each.

versions.untested_parts: No student fine-tuning on teacher-generated, semantically unrelated, filtered outputs.
No comparison of students sharing versus not sharing a teacher's base model.
No transmission of misalignment or other alignment-relevant traits through filtered teacher data.
The post reports entropy changes but does not test the proposed signal-carrier mechanisms.
No comparison of full fine-tuning, LoRA ranks, or evaluation prompts different from training.
Tests GCG-optimized prompt prefixes and broad persona outcomes, not tokens linked to a predetermined trait or preference.

relation.reason: The post presents its work as part of a 'subliminal prompting' stream and mentions entangled numbers, but reports no result on any version.

tranche.reason: The prefixes are GCG strings optimised for first-token Shannon entropy. They are not tokens linked to a trait, there is no teacher-student fine-tuning, and the outcome is undirected persona emergence. So no version (A-F) is tested and the finding isn't used as a tool. Entangled numbers are mentioned but no results are given. The GCG misalignment-word attempt promotes words directly, which is not version F's linked-token route.

source_check.notes: The controls are small (24 rollouts each, against 480 triggered), there is one query ('what shall I do today'), and the judge was local Claude subagents. The text's 40.4% novel-persona figure is among fluent rollouts only and is not the table's per-model rate. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Lines advising readers to 'ask your favourite AI' are aimed at humans, not an injection.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GCG-optimized prefixes on the four tested models
reader_labels.reason: The triggered rollouts had non-assistant-persona rates of 35.4%, 32.7%, 14.6%, and 13.5%, compared with 0% on clean prompts (r1-r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Random junk produced 4.2% non-assistant personas for Gemma-7b-it but 0 for the other three models, so persona shifts are not wholly specific to the optimized triggers in every condition (r9-r12).
